Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  2-day history of mid-lower abdominal pain; increased urinary frequency; pink-tinged urine; mild nausea; feels hot/sweaty. No known chronic conditions. Alcohol use (≈4 beers/week).  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Mother—early breast cancer. No other family history recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  No regular medications. Antibiotic prescribed today (name/dose/route not documented) for 3 days.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Regular menses; no inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding; prior contraceptive implant removed 1 yr ago; no vaginal discharge reported.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Non-smoker; drinks ~1 beer on 4 days/week; physical activity and diet not recorded; no illicit drug use recorded.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Female with new-onset suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and visible hematuria without dysuria, fever, or flank pain.  
- Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (lower urinary tract infection). Supported by location of pain, frequency, hematuria, mild systemic features, and absence of flank pain (DDx step3—high likelihood).  
- Considerations:  
  • Urolithiasis (medium likelihood)—hematuria and nausea could reflect distal ureteric stone; monitor for colicky pain or flank radiation.  
  • Early appendicitis (low-medium likelihood)—unlikely but consider if pain migrates or systemic signs develop.  
- Management: Oral antibiotic course prescribed (twice daily for 3 days; specific agent not documented). Safety-net advice given—seek review if worsening pain, fever, back pain, or recurrence. Telehealth follow-up or face-to-face exam if no improvement.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Brief counselling on need for prompt review if symptoms worsen; no broader prevention discussion recorded.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of abdominal pain and urinary symptoms (implied).  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded (acute issue).  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  None at this consultation.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Advise to contact service if symptoms worsen or recur; no scheduled appointment documented.

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: Suprapubic pain, frequency, hematuria, minimal systemic signs.  
2. Urolithiasis (renal/ureteric stone) – Medium likelihood: Hematuria and nausea could represent distal stone though pain character atypical.  
3. Early appendicitis – Low-Medium likelihood: Early central abdominal pain and mild nausea but urinary features make this less likely.
